rows.title_full: AN ACT DESIGNATING THE PHILIPPINE PHILHARMONIC ORCHESTRA AS THE NATIONAL ORCHESTRA OF THE PHILIPPINES, DEFINING ITS ROLE AND FUNCTIONS AS SUCH, APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: In recognition of its efforts and numerous awards it has received for and in behalf of the Philippines, the Philippine Philharmonic Orchestra (PPO) is designated as the country's national orchestra. The bill grants the orchestra and its members certain benefits, such as exemption from civil service laws; free use of office space, rehearsal free use of office space, rehearsal studios, and production and technical facilities at the CCP; and travel and project grants for research, documentation, and production from the National Commission for Culture and the Arts (NCCA). On the other hand, the PPO will be mandated to, among others, recruit and develop new talents from all over the country; and disseminate, produce, and preserve Philippine mussic and prepare and set new, superior and serious goals for the new millenium for national performances and international tours.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on BASIC EDUCATION since 2000-08-21

Also inclided are programs for continuous education and training and adequate salary and benefits. This proposed Magna Carta for the Philippine National Police attempts to properly address the existing loopholes and inadequacies of the present system and laws governing the PNP structure, organization and oepration. rows.abstract: "National Health Facilities Enhancement Act of 2000." Rationale: Most stakeholders in the national health services observed that Philippine health service has suffered tremendous damage after the devolution of health services to the Local GovernmentUnits (LGUs) and which to them is the most destructive event to basic health services in recent times. Naturally, the already inadequate health services deteriorated even further when national government funds and personnel were withdrawn resultingin a fragmented delivery of health services, with a dangerous gap between hospital care and preventive public health services; weak preventive medicine; and the removal of effective referral services and networking among health facilities. Today, itappears that the bulk of the burden of shouldering the high cost of health care remained at the hands of the individual families who can't afford the prohibitive cost of preserving their health.

rows.abstract: Rationale: While it may be argued that the Rural Electric Cooperatives (RECs) may register with the Cooperative Development authority (CDA) to be able to avail of exemptions from the coverage of real property taxes, the hundreds of RECs have not done so for a myriad of reasons. Hence, the real property taxes assessed and levied by the LGUs upon the RECs. > To eliminate this aberration, the attached measure seeks to amend the Local Government Code by exempting the RECs from the coverage of realproperty taxes. True, the LGUs will be deprived of income, but this deprivation will in the long term spare the consumers from paying higher power rates and redound to the benefit of everyone concerned.

rows.abstract: This bill provides for the following: (1) ALL ACCREDITED BARANGAY HEALTH WORKERS SHALL BE ENTITLED TO A MONTHLY HONORARIA OF TWO THOUSAND PESOS (P2,000.00); (2) INSURANCE COVERAGE - ALL BARANGAY HEALTH WORKERS ARE GRANTED INSURANCE COVERAGE BY THE GOVERNMENT SERVICE INSURANCE SYSTEM OR ANY ACCREDITED INSURANCE COMPANY IN AN AMOUNT NOT LESS THAN TEN THOUSAND PESOS (P10,000.00).
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on HEALTH since 2000-08-30

rows.author: A041
rows.title_full: AN ACT ALLOWING TAX INCENTIVES TO PRIVATE EDUCATION INSTITUTIONS FOR NON-IMPOSITION OF INCREASES IN SCHOOL FEES
rows.abstract: As a general rule, any instition of learning duly recongized by the appropriate education agency and which did not avail of any tuition fee rate increase or adjustment for a particular school year to support its operation shall be EXEMPT from the payment of taxes of income from all sources, including interest from deposits and yield from substitutes or trust funds, for the applicable school or fiscal year only.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on WAYS AND MEANS since 2000-08-30

rows.title_full: AN ACT UPGRADING THE EXISTING FACILITIES OF THE VETERANS MEMORIAL MEDICAL CENTER (VMMC) THROUGH A FIVE (5)-YEAR MODERNIZATION PLAN AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.abstract: This bill seeks to modernize and upgrade the existing facilities of the Veterans Memorial Medical Center (VMMC) through the VMMC Five-Year Modernization Plan.  The VMMC is envisioned to be equipped with modern health equipment and facilities which shall include well-trained medical staff and other personnel to attend to the health and other medical needs of the veterans. This is one way of showing our concern for, and acknowledgment of the sacrifices and heroic deeds of our veterans.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on  since 2000-08-30

rows.author: C028
rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING ARTICLE 26 OF THE NEW CIVIL CODE TO INCLUDE AS ACTIONABLE WRONG THE DISCLOSING OR CIRCULATING TO THIRD PARTIES A MAILING LIST OF PERSONAL INFORMATION OF PERSON GIVEN IN CONFIDENCE
rows.abstract: The following act shall produce a cause of action for damages, prevention and other relief: DISCLOSING, DISTRIBUTING, CIRCULATING AND/OR TRANSMITTING, WITH OR WITHOUT CONSIDERATION, TO THIRD PARTIES THROUGH A MAILING LIST USED FOR COMMERCIAL PURPOSES PERSONAL INFORMATION GIVEN BY ANOTHER, INCLUDING, BUT NOT LIMITED TO, THE PERSON'S NAME, RESIDENTIAL/BUS INESS ADDRESS AND CONTRACT INFORMATION, WHICH INFORMATION IS PRESUMED TO HAVE BEEN GIVEN IN CONFIDENCE.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on REVISION OF LAWS since 2000-08-30

rows.author: A067
rows.title_full: AN ACT REQUIRING THE INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY OFFICE (IPO) TO REMIT ITS EARNINGS OR REVENUES ANNUALLY TO THE NATIONAL GOVERNMENT, AMENDING FOR THIS PURPOSE SECTION 14 OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 8293
rows.abstract: It is the policy of the State that in order for the National Government to realize additional revenues and, as a result, free more resources for priority development programs and projects, revenue-earning government agencies, without impairing theirability to pursue the goals for which they have been established, shall share a substantial amount of their net earnings with the National Government.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on TRADE AND INDUSTRY since 2000-08-30

rows.author: A067
rows.title_full: AN ACT REQUIRING THE GARMENTS AND TEXTILE EXPORT BOARD (GTEB) TO REMIT ITS EARNINGS OR REVENUES ANNUALLY TO THE NATIONAL GOVERNMENT, AMENDING FOR THIS PURPOSE SECTION 4 OF EXECUTIVE ORDER NUMBERED 952
rows.abstract: The bill seeks to require the Garments and Textile Export Board (GTEB) to publicly declare its income and remit to the National Government all of its earnings yearly in order to help address the government deficit and make more scarce resources available for priority devleopment projects.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on TRADE AND INDUSTRY since 2000-08-30

rows.author: A067
rows.title_full: AN ACT MANDATING THAT ALL REMITTANCES MADE ANNUALLY BY PHILIPPINE NATIONAL OIL COMPANY (PNOC) TO THE NATIONAL GOVERNMENT UNDER REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7656, FOR THE FOUR (4) YEARS IMMEDIATELY FOLLOWING THE APPROVAL OF THIS ACT, BE COMMITTED EXCLUSIVELY TOTHE RURAL ELECTRIFICATION PROGRAM AND DISBURSED IN ACCORDANCE WITH THE PRIORITIES SET BY THE DEPARTMENT OF ENERGY (DOE) AND THE NATIONAL ELECTRIFICATION ADMINISTRATION (NEA)
rows.abstract: The bill seeks to assure that all the dividends remitted by the Philippine National Oil Company (PNOC) to the National Government are applied exclusively to the furtherance of the Rural Electrification Program (REP) over the next four (4) years in order to ultimately stimulate, promote and sustain much needed economic growth in the Philippine countryside.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on APPROPRIATIONS since 2000-08-30

rows.author: A087
rows.title_full: AN ACT PENALIZING ACTIVITIES INIMICAL TO THE USE OF CYBERSPACE, DESTRUCTION OF INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY INFRASTRUCTURE AND RELATED OFFENSES
rows.abstract: It is the policy of the State to protect society against computer fraudm destruction of electronic systems and properties and proliferation of cyber-crime brought about by the continuing globalication of computer networks.  It is imperative that theconfidentiality , integrity, reliability and availability of computer systems, networks and computer data are maintained in the furtherance of our national interest and security.  It is in this context that the State recognize its duty to safeguardits interest against the menance of electronic fraud and other instruments of high technology that tend to disrupt peace and order in cyberspace.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY since 2000-08-30
